title: Payments at an official’s request, and Board files naming the payor or the recipient within a year
question: When a supervisor or mayor asked someone to pay a third party, did the payor have a contract, grant or lease before that official around the same time, and was the recipient then funded by the Board?
finding: The reports for 2015 to 2023 give 324 named organizations as payor or recipient of a payment requested by a supervisor or mayor. For 29 of them a Board file naming the organization was decided within a year either side of the payment; moving each payment two years earlier or later gives 29, so the closeness in time is about what the Board’s routine yearly files would give. In 49 payment-and-file pairs the official who asked also sponsored the file, voted on it or was Mayor on the day (9 where the payor had the file, 0 where the recipient was then paid by the City, 40 where the recipient then made a gift the Board accepted); 14 of those fall within 90 days. The largest within 90 days: $385,000 paid to San Francisco Parks Alliance at Mark Farrell’s request on 2017-10-31, and File 171116 (grant the City accepts) decided 42 days later, on which the official is recorded as: voted yes (10 to 0).
how: Payments are the State Form 803 reports (2015 to 2018) and Form 3610b filings (2019 to 2023), as the “officials” analysis reads them, for officials on this project’s roster of supervisors and mayors. Payors and recipients that do not read as an organization are left out, as are public bodies. Each organization is looked up by exact name among the counterparties of passed Board money files; a file is near when its final Board roll call (or, without one, its recorded passage) is within 365 days of the payment. For a recipient only files that follow the payment are listed, and the row says whether the file pays the recipient (a contract, grant agreement, lease or loan) or records a gift from the recipient that the Board accepted for a department. “Days” is the decision date minus the payment date, so a negative number means the Board acted first. The comparison repeats the look-up with every payment date moved 730 days each way and averages the two.
limits: Requested payments reported on these forms were permitted and disclosed at the time; since January 2022 asking an interested party is barred without a waiver, and the forms stop in early 2023. An organization with a contract renewed every year always has a file within a year of anything. Three Form 3610b filings by the youth department list nonprofits that received money as “payors”; a row resting on them shows the grant, not a gift. The everyday reason for a real pair is that officials ask the companies and foundations they already know.
